core.title: Keep a connected family-kind definition anchor for every core domain artifact
core.given: Core domain artifacts: theme, train, interlocking, wagon, feature, wmbt, artifact.
core.when: You change planner convention nodes or relationship edges, or the anchor validator reports a finding.
core.then: Each core domain artifact must have a definition-anchor node of kind family, identified per the profile's anchor id scheme (idiom.definition_anchor_id), that is a source_ref or target_ref of at least one relationship edge; a missing, non-family or orphan anchor is refused.
prefer: Author a missing anchor as a definition-anchor node file placed and named per the profile's anchor-node file pattern (layout.definition_anchor_file), with kind family, then wire at least one relationship edge from it.
avoid: Making an anchor kind rule/constraint or binding a validator to it; it is transitively protected by the constraint/rule nodes it requires.
Creating the anchor but leaving it an orphan.
unless: Only the seven core domain artifacts must carry an anchor; other conventions are unaffected.
core.why: The anchor gives each core artifact a stable meaning without binding a validator; it must both exist (this rule) and be graph-connected (the convention graph's no-orphan-nodes rule).
evidence: For each of theme, train, interlocking, wagon, feature, wmbt, artifact: its definition-anchor node exists, has kind family, and appears as source_ref or target_ref of at least one edge in the relationship graph.
verification: The core artifact set is exactly seven: theme, train, interlocking, wagon, feature, wmbt, artifact; the expected anchor node for each is identified by the profile's anchor id scheme.
Refuse when an anchor node is missing, when its kind is not family, or when it is an orphan (not a source_ref/target_ref of any edge).
Disposition strict (a violation is refused); severity 3.

Terms: a definition anchor is a node of kind family that gives a core domain artifact a stable meaning without binding a validator (an advisory semantic anchor); a core domain artifact is one of the seven planner domain-decomposition artifacts.
Pairs with the convention graph's no-orphan-nodes rule: the anchor must both exist (this rule) and be graph-connected.
The anchor binds no validator itself; it is transitively protected by the constraint/rule nodes it requires.
Do not require anchors for conventions outside the seven core artifacts (exception scope); the check reports pre-existing violations regardless of what the current change touched.

values: any file located under the convention-graph tree supplied by the profile key layout.convention_graph — the file need not itself be a convention node or a relationship edge; a documentation, configuration or other file in that tree also activates this rule
any planner convention node added, removed, renamed or re-kinded
any relationship edge added, removed or rewired
the anchor validator reports a missing, non-family or orphan definition anchor for a core artifact

fires: The planner deletes or renames a core artifact's definition-anchor node.
The planner changes an anchor's kind from family to rule or constraint.
The planner removes or rewires relationship edges (including edges whose other end is a non-core node) so that a core artifact's anchor is no longer a source_ref or target_ref of any edge.
The anchor validator reports that one of the seven core artifacts already lacks an anchor, has a non-family anchor, or has an orphan anchor, even if the current task did not cause it.
doesNotFire: Demanding a definition anchor for a convention that is not one of the seven core domain artifacts.
Work confined to coder or tester conventions while all seven planner anchors exist, are kind family, and are graph-connected.

profileRequirements.meaning: Path or glob of the planner convention-graph tree, where planner convention nodes and relationship edges live. This rule's file activation fact matches EVERY file under this tree — not only convention node or relationship-edge files — and the anchor nodes themselves live inside it; instantiating this key with the Bun value selects exactly the entire Bun path glob.
How a definition-anchor node is identified in the convention graph: the expected node id scheme for each core domain artifact, used by the verifier to locate the anchor.
Path pattern of one definition-anchor node file inside the convention-graph tree — the concrete authoring location and file naming of an anchor node, used by the core's fix recipe.

proposedKeys.meaning: Path or glob of the ATDD convention-graph tree, where planner convention nodes and relationship edges live; rule activations that scope to the convention graph match every file under this tree (not only node or edge files).
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: No existing key locates the convention graph: roles.plan_artifact.path and roots.plan point at the plan root where plan items (e.g. WMBTs) live, while the planner conventions tree sits under the source root.

proposedKeys.meaning: The concrete construct by which a definition-anchor node is identified in the convention graph: the expected node id scheme per core domain artifact.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: The urn group covers artifact URNs (component, acceptance, train, wmbt, wagon, feature, journey...), not convention-graph node ids, and no idiom key exists for the anchor node naming scheme.

proposedKeys.meaning: Path pattern of one definition-anchor node file inside the convention-graph tree: the subdirectory where anchor nodes are authored and the node file-name pattern (id plus file suffix).
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: layout.plan_item is the path of a plan artifact under the plan root; layout.convention_graph locates only the enclosing tree and idiom.definition_anchor_id only the node id — none gives the nodes subdirectory or the node-file name/suffix pattern needed to author an anchor.

neutralityNotes: The convention-graph model itself — nodes with kinds family/rule/constraint, relationship edges with source_ref/target_ref endpoints, the seven core domain artifacts, and the planner/coder/tester roles — is treated as shared ATDD method vocabulary and kept in the core rather than moved to the profile; if a future stack renames the node-kind taxonomy or edge endpoint roles, an idiom key would be needed for them. Three concrete things the core needs had no existing vocabulary key and are proposed: the convention-graph tree location (layout.convention_graph, which also binds this rule's file activation to EVERY file under the tree — not only convention node or relationship-edge files — so the Bun instantiation selects exactly the entire src/atdd/planner/conventions/** glob rather than a narrower node/edge subset or all plan-artifact files), the anchor node id scheme (idiom.definition_anchor_id), and the anchor-node authoring file path/name pattern (layout.definition_anchor_file). Remaining realization-specific tooling — the `atdd author relationship` CLI command, the validator/test finding id, and the paired rule id planner.relationship.no-orphan-nodes — stays bunOnly; the core's verification names the check and the pairing generically, and severity 3 / strict disposition stay in core verification per the notProfileKeys rule.
